sentences.text: 1. Appellants/claimants have preferred this miscellaneous appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 (in short "MV Act") for enhancement of the compensation amount awarded in Claim Case No.30/14 passed by the Member, MACT, Ratlam vide Award dated 2.2.2015, whereby an amount of compensation of Rs.7,01,000/- has been awarded to the claimants.

2. The relevant and necessary facts of the case, in brief, are that on 13.1.2014 at about 7.30 p.m.
deceased Amrit Bhil was going on the motorcycle with due care at normal speed.

Respondent No.1 who is the driver of the offending vehicle bearing Registration No.MP09-KC-4348 driven the vehicle rashly and negligently and hit the deceased's motorcycle, due to which deceased sustained fatal injuries and he has NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:23373 been died on the spot.
Matter ha been reported against the respondent No.1 at P.S. Bilpank.
Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and vehicle was insured with respondent No.3/insurance company.
Claimant No.1 Basanti Bai is the widow of the deceased and Claimant No.2 Ravina is daughter of the deceased and claimants No.3 & 4 Soma and Savri Bai are the parents of the deceased.

Claimants have preferred a petition under Section 166 of the MV Act before the below Tribunal by stating that at the time of accident deceased Amrit Bhil was aged about 22 years and he used to earn Rs.25,000/- per month from the agriculture.
Claimants were dependent upon the income of the deceased and after the death of deceased Amrit they have been deprived from his income.

Therefore,
they prayed for compensation of Rs.19,05,000/- with the interest.

sentences.text: 3. Respondents No.1 and 2 admits in their written statement that respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and vehicle was insured with respondent No.3/insurance company, but they have denied all other claim averments.

4. Respondent No.3/insurance company denied all the claim averments by submitting in its written statement that at the time of accident respondent No.1 was not having any valid and effective driving licence and vehicle owner was also not having permit and fitness certificate.
Therefore, due to the breach of terms of the insurance policy, insurance company is not liable for any compensation.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:23373 5.

On the basis of the aforesaid pleadings learned below Tribunal has framed issued and after recording and appreciating the evidence available on record, partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation of Rs.7,01,000/- in favour of the claimants No.1 and 2, but no compensation has been awarded in favour of the appellants No.1 & 2/claimants No.3 & 4 by holding that they are getting income from the agricultural land which belongs to the deceased.
Being aggrieved by the findings given by the below Tribunal, this appeal has been preferred before this Court by the appellants.

6. Learned counsel for the appellants contended that the claims tribunal has committed legal and factual error by not considering the actual income of the deceased and income of the deceased assessed by the below Tribunal is on much lower side, which is against the evidence available on record.
Considering the age of the deceased 50% future prospects should be added.

The below tribunal has committed error in granting too low and meager amount under various heads i.e.
funeral expenses, loss of love and affection, loss of estate, conveyance charges, loss of expectancy of life, mental pain and suffering.

Appellants No.1 & 2 are the old aged parents of the deceased, who were dependent upon income of the deceased, therefore, deduction of 1/4th should be applied and appellants No.1 & 2 are also entitled for their share in the awarded amount.
Hence, he prays for enhancement of the compensation amount.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:23373 7.
Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3 opposes the prayer and prays for its rejection by supporting the impugned award passed by the below Tribunal.

8. At the time of final arguments nobody appeared on behalf of respondents No.1, 2 & 4.
9.
I have heard the arguments advanced by both the parties and perused the record with due care.

10. From perusal of the evidence available on record, it is established from the oral as well as documentary evidence that the aforesaid accident took place by the offending vehicle, which was being driven by respondent No.1 rashly and negligently and at the time of accident the said vehicle was duly insured with the respondent No.3 and respondent No.2 is owner of the offending vehicle.
There is no evidence available on record to establish that there was any breach of insurance policy committed by the owner or driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the insurance company along with the respondents No.1 & 2 is liable to pay the compensation amount.

sentences.text: The moot question to be addressed in this appeal preferred by the appellants is, as to whether the below Tribunal was justified in awarding compensation of Rs.7,01,000/- to the claimants and appellants No.1 & 2 are also entitled for their share in the compensation amount being parents of the deceased?
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:23373 12.
Claimant Basanti Bai (AW-1) has been examined before the below tribunal.

She categorically stated in her statement that her husband Amritlal was doing agriculture work and earning Rs.25,000/- per month, but she admits in her cross-examination that no agriculture land was found in the name of her husband and the agricultural land described in the revenue record (Ex.A-11 &
A-12) belongs to her father- in-law Soma and she did not produce any relevant document regarding sale of the agriculture crop by her husband.
She admits that about 1-2 years ago her husband earned Rs.100/- wages from labour work.
Therefore, the below tribunal has rightly assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.3,000/- per month.
13. But in the instant case there are four claimants, therefore, 1/4th should be deducted for self expenses of the deceased instead of 1/3rd.

Below tribunal has awarded only Rs.1,00,000/- to the claimant No.1 under the head of loss of consortium but each of the claimant is entitled to get Rs.40,000/- under the head of loss of consortium, therefore, amount of Rs.60,000/- deserves to be enhanced under the head of loss of consortium.

14. From perusal of the impugned award, it appears that although below tribunal has held that the appellants No.1 & 2 are the parents of the deceased, but below tribunal has held that they are having sufficient agricultural land and means of income, therefore, they cannot be considered dependent upon their deceased son Amrit.

But the claimant Basanti (AW-1) categorically stated in her statement that she is still NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:23373 living with her father-in-law at village Mudadi and she is also doing work in the agriculture field.
She categorically admits in para-3 of her deposition that prior to the accident her husband was doing agriculture work and all the claimants were dependent upon income of her husband.

Therefore, the finding given by the below tribunal appears to be erroneous and on the basis of the statement of Basanti Bai it has been proved that appellants No.1 & 2 are also dependent upon the deceased and they are also entitled to get their share in the awarded amount.

15. In view of the foregoing discussion, the compensation awarded by the below Tribunal is modified as under:-
(1) Loss of dependency - Rs.6,31,800/-
(Rs.3,000/- x 12 (-) 1/4th deduction towards self expenses (+) 30% future prospects x 18 multiplier)
(2) Funeral expenses - Rs.25,000/-
(3) Loss of consortium (Rs.40,000 x 4) - Rs.1,60,000/-
Soma vs Deepak on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35290904/
3
Therefore, the appellants are entitled to get total compensation of Rs.8,16,800/-, whereas the below tribunal has awarded only a sum of Rs.7,01,000/-.

Therefore, the appellants are entitled to get the enhancement amount of Rs.1,15,800/-.
14.
In the result, the appeal is partly allowed.
The compensation as awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be and is accordingly enhanced by a sum of Rs.1,15,800/-.
All the four claimants shall be entitled to get equal share of 25% in the total compensation amount.
The enhanced NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:23373 amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the below Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the below Tribunal shall remain intact.
Both the parties shall bear their own expenses.
C.C. as per rules.
(ANIL VERMA)
JUDGE Trilok/- TRILOK SINGH SAVNER
